deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages). Sigma is a system of n pseudo-lines D_i in a real projective plane X, assumed generic: the vertices s_alpha = D_i ∩ D_j are simple. X^∨ is the dual plane, i.e. the space of (pseudo-)lines. Each line D_i is a point delta_i of X^∨, and each vertex s_alpha of Sigma is a line Delta_alpha in X^∨, namely the pencil of lines through s_alpha, which joins delta_i and delta_j. This gives an arrangement of n(n-1)/2 lines in X^∨. Its 'super-singular' vertices are the delta_i, each of multiplicity n-1. After a small perturbation, all its other vertices are double points.

A face F of this dual arrangement is a combinatorial class of lines D = D_F avoiding all vertices of Sigma, i.e. a 'cut' of Sigma. An edge a_alpha of F, lying on Delta_alpha, corresponds to a specialization D -> D_alpha in which D passes through s_alpha. The previous page asked to interpret the 'structure polygonale' of the faces (their edges and vertices) in terms of Sigma; this page begins that.

Step 1: orientations. Grothendieck notes a correspondence between orientations of the 2-cell F and orientations of the line D. For genuine lines this is canonical. If D = P(L), with L a 2-dimensional subspace of a 3-dimensional space V, then T_delta X^∨ = Hom(L, V/L) = L^* ⊗ V/L. Its determinant is det(L^*) ⊗ (V/L)^{⊗2}, so an orientation of T_delta X^∨ is the same as an orientation of L, hence of P(L) = D. The correspondence is continuous in delta.

Step 2: transport. Carrying the orientation of F continuously across an edge a_alpha into the adjacent face F' corresponds to the continuous ('parallel') transport of the orientation of D during the sweep ('balayage') in which D moves across s_alpha. He says the drawing makes the 'naive' choice of orientation transports plausible. This bears on the earlier problem of 'circuits', in particular the super-singular circuits around the delta_i, where the previous page found the current recipe unsatisfactory.

Step 3: a remark on coverings. He compares the covering obtained from the natural maps 𝔛 -> X (𝔛 is presumably an incidence or flag space) with the one given by the natural map X^∨ -> X. The reading of this sentence is uncertain.

Step 4: the walk along a_alpha (bottom right, continued on the next page). Start from omega_F (which gives omega_D) and an edge a_alpha (which gives a vertex s_alpha). Move in a straight line from delta_0 in F to a point delta_1 near a_alpha. In X this means: choose a point x on D and a local orientation at x, then pivot D about x in the given sense until D_1 passes through s_alpha. Moving along a_alpha then means D_1 pivots about s_alpha. The edge a_alpha ends at a vertex delta_2 = Delta_alpha ∩ Delta_beta, the first moment the pivoting line meets another vertex s_beta. So the segment structure of a_alpha is the sequence of vertices s_beta met while rotating the pencil at s_alpha, restricted to the cut. The bottom figure is a sweep picture: the yellow line D = D_delta, dashed D_1 and D_2, red pseudo-lines, the shaded triangles of specialization, and segments a'_alpha.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. The orientation correspondence F <-> D is asserted without proof. It is canonical for straight lines; for pseudo-lines it needs a topological model of the dual space (continuity of the family of pseudo-lines), which is not addressed here.

The sign of the rotation about s_alpha is left 'à expliciter'. The next page finds an 'anticompatibility' of orientations at the contact flag (s_alpha, D_1), so the 'naive' transport needs a sign correction there.

ideas.what: Duality of a pseudo-line arrangement: vertices of Sigma become lines of the dual plane, lines become points, and faces of the dual arrangement are combinatorial types of transversal lines (cuts).
ideas.modern_name: Duality for (pseudo)line arrangements; allowable sequences / sweeps; dual topological projective plane

ideas.what: Canonical correspondence between local orientations of the dual plane at delta and orientations of the line D, compatible with continuous transport.
ideas.modern_name: T_[L] Gr(2,3) = Hom(L, V/L), giving or(T) ≅ or(L); oriented lines form the double cover S^2 -> RP^2

ideas.what: Crossing an edge of a dual face equals a sweep of D across a vertex. Moving along a dual edge equals rotating the pencil at s_alpha; the edge's endpoints are the next vertices met.
ideas.modern_name: Topological sweep / rotational sweep (mutations of allowable sequences)

ideas.what: Comparison of the coverings given by the natural maps 𝔛 -> X and X^∨ -> X, used to control orientation transports and 'circuits'.
ideas.modern_name: Orientation double covers of the incidence (flag) variety

missed.claim: Programme to read off the polygonal (edge/vertex) structure of each cell of the dual arrangement from rotations about vertices of Sigma, with orientation bookkeeping chosen so that transport around super-singular circuits behaves well. The page leaves the sign convention open and only calls the 'naive' choice 'plausible'.
missed.quote: Le dessin paraît rendre plausible le choix "naïf" des transports d'orientation
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only marginally: the combinatorics itself is standard (sweeps, allowable sequences). The orientation/monodromy bookkeeping around the multiple points delta_i might be relevant to sign conventions in oriented-matroid or real-discriminant studies, but nothing new is established here.

deep.surprise_reason: A working page. It translates elementary duality between a pseudo-line arrangement and its dual, plus orientation transport, into sweep language. The ideas are standard in discrete geometry (Goodman–Pollack); the open sign question is local bookkeeping.
transcription_corrections: 'au sens des bandes correspondantes' should read 'au sens des balayages correspondants' (the word 'balayage' recurs on the page).
'(le long de a_α disons)' and '(ou "parallèle")' are correct.
'(↦ [-sa-] sommet de Σ)' reads '(↦ son sommet s_α de Σ)' or '↦ un sommet de Σ'.
Last lines of the left column: 'Le fait qu'on obtienne ... par les applications naturelles 𝔛 → X se rapproche[?] du fait qu'on a ... par l'application naturelle X^∨ → X'. 'revêtement' is uncertain.
Bottom right: 'i.e. faisons pivoter... [-p-]choisissons un pt x sur D et une orientation du voisinage en x, et faisons pivoter'.
'D = D_δ' in the figure is likely D = D_{δ_0}.
'des variétés à p.v. stables ou bandes' is probably '... par balayage'; the exact reading is uncertain.
